phases.name: Frame the contract and ingress
phases.description: Separate stated behavior from operating constraints, record unknowns, and establish authenticated, bounded entry points.

phases.name: Persist and serve comment threads
phases.description: Keep durable comment state authoritative, model replies and reactions, and make large reads cursor-based with a cache that can be bypassed.

phases.name: Moderate and publish approved events
phases.description: Use durable moderation work and a transactional outbox so only committed, policy-approved changes reach live subscribers.

phases.name: Operate under failures and viral load
phases.description: Choose safe outage behavior, scale from measured bottlenecks, and observe moderation, persistence, queueing, cache, and delivery health.

steps.title: Separate functional behavior from operating constraints
steps.content: Functional requirements in the frozen brief are: post and view comments in real time; support nested replies; like and reply to comments; edit and delete comments; filter spam and profanity; and paginate large threads. The brief also calls for viral posts with thousands of comments and millions of comments per day. Treat those as scale requirements, not measured capacity targets. Nonfunctional requirements and constraints are real-time updates, high write throughput, chronological and top ordering, moderation capability, and low-latency updates. No numeric latency, peak rate, availability, retention, or recovery target is supplied, so do not invent one. The requirement and constraint anchors below refer to the fixture's exact array positions.

steps.title: Write down assumptions and questions
steps.content: Assume the existing Facebook identity and post-visibility systems provide a verified actor and authorize access to each post; the comment service must still check author and moderator permissions for every mutation and subscription. Assume a durable database can commit a comment and its outbox record atomically, but validate the selected engine's transaction and partition behavior. The author may see their own comment as pending; other viewers see only approved comments. The brief does not define top-ranking semantics, maximum reply depth, edit conflict policy, retention, peak traffic, SLOs, or moderation policy. Confirm those with product and operations before sizing or promising behavior. These are explicit design assumptions, not additional problem requirements.

steps.title: Choose stable pagination and defer undefined ranking
steps.content: A cursor must remain meaningful while new comments arrive. Use a stable keyset cursor over the selected order and a unique tie-breaker; do not use offset pagination for deep or rapidly changing threads. The prompt names chronological and top ordering but does not define a top score or freshness window.

decision.question: How should the first version expose ordering?
decision.chosen: Offer chronological ordering with a stable keyset cursor; define and validate the top-ranking formula with product before enabling that mode.
decision.chosenReason: Chronological order is implementable from the stated brief. Inventing a ranking formula would create an unsupported product promise and unstable cursors.

alternatives.option: Sort every page by a live, global score
alternatives.tradeoff: Ranking semantics and write amplification are unspecified, and concurrent score changes can move rows between pages.

alternatives.option: Expose chronological order only and close the top-ordering question
alternatives.tradeoff: The constraint explicitly names top ordering, so the unresolved product decision remains visible rather than being silently dropped.

steps.title: Add the comment client
steps.content: The existing web and mobile clients render approved comments, thread replies, likes, edit/delete controls allowed to the actor, and the current moderation state to the author. They request bounded pages and establish an authenticated live subscription only while the viewer can access the post.

component.label: Facebook Comment Clients
component.description: Thread UI, paged reads, mutations, and live subscriptions

properties.purpose: Render authorized comment threads and moderation state, submit idempotent create/edit/delete/like actions, page with opaque cursors, and reconnect to live updates only for posts the viewer may access.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Web App catalog component for the customer-facing client.

steps.title: Add the authenticated API boundary
steps.content: Expose bounded HTTP operations for thread reads and mutations, plus an authenticated WebSocket upgrade or subscription path. Validate post and comment identifiers, payload size, cursor shape, and caller identity; enforce post visibility and mutation permissions in the service as well as at ingress.

component.label: Comment API Gateway

properties.purpose: Terminate TLS, authenticate HTTP and WebSocket requests, validate bounded comment payloads and cursors, apply coarse request limits, and pass verified identity context to the comment service.

component.highlightReason: Uses the catalog API Gateway; no new protocol-specific component is introduced.

steps.title: Connect the client to the API
steps.content: Use HTTPS for page reads and mutations. The create request carries a client-generated idempotency key so a retry after a timeout cannot create a second comment or like.

connection.label: HTTPS reads and mutations
connection.description: Authenticated, bounded requests with opaque cursors and idempotency keys.

steps.title: Add per-actor and per-post admission controls
steps.content: Apply limits by authenticated actor and post, with a separate coarse IP limit for unauthenticated connection attempts. Use bounded request sizes and admission control to protect the write path. Rate limiting reduces abuse and overload; it is not a substitute for spam/profanity moderation and must not silently discard accepted comments.

component.label: Comment Admission Limits

properties.purpose: Apply configurable actor, post, and connection quotas with bounded request sizes and explicit retry responses; protect hot posts and backend capacity without replacing content moderation or silently dropping accepted writes.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Rate Limiter catalog component for configurable admission control.

steps.title: Pass admitted requests to the service
steps.content: The gateway applies the coarse request checks first; actor- and post-aware limits then run with verified identity context before the service performs reads or mutations. Return a clear retry response when admission is denied.

connection.label: Verified request context
connection.description: Actor/post-aware quotas and explicit overload responses before application work.

steps.title: Add the comment service
steps.content: Keep the service stateless where practical. Implement create/read/reply/like/edit/delete operations, permission checks, moderation-state transitions, cursor validation, and idempotency. A reply stores its parent and root identifiers; a like is unique per actor and comment. Never report a comment as published before its durable state is committed.

component.label: Comment and Thread Service
component.description: Authorized comment lifecycle and bounded thread queries

properties.purpose: Enforce post visibility and actor permissions; implement idempotent create, reply, like, edit, delete, and cursor reads; manage moderation status and versioned tombstones; and commit durable state before acknowledging a write.

component.highlightReason: Uses the catalog Backend Server for the domain API and lifecycle rules.

steps.title: Connect admitted traffic to the comment service
steps.content: Forward only requests that pass ingress validation and admission checks. The service remains the final authorization boundary because gateway policies can be stale or incomplete.

connection.label: Admitted comment API
connection.description: Validated requests with identity context; service rechecks authorization.

steps.title: Add authoritative comment storage
steps.content: Persist comments, parent/root links, actor-comment like uniqueness, edit versions, moderation status, and an outbox in the same transaction as each state change. Plan indexes for `(post_id, created_at, comment_id)` and `(post_id, root_id, created_at, comment_id)`. Partition and shard hot posts only after measured peak-rate and query tests; a sharded chronological page needs a deterministic merge and cursor over every participating shard.

component.label: Comment System of Record
component.description: Durable comments, reactions, moderation state, and outbox

properties.purpose: Authoritatively persist comment text and status, post/parent/root identifiers, unique actor-comment likes, versioned edits and tombstones, and transactional outbox rows; support post/time and post/root/time keyset access patterns with measured hot-key partitioning.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Database component and records storage semantics in its supported purpose field.

steps.title: Connect service reads and writes to durable storage
steps.content: Commit comment state, moderation state, and the corresponding outbox intent atomically. Use deterministic IDs and conditional writes for idempotency. A cache entry or broker message alone is never proof that a comment was committed.

connection.label: Authoritative reads and transactions
connection.description: Idempotent comment mutations and transactional outbox; cursor-based thread queries.

steps.title: Keep the data model explicit about thread and order
steps.content: Use parent_id and root_id for reply traversal and stable comment IDs as pagination tie-breakers. If a reply-depth limit or top-ranking score is required, confirm the product rule; neither is specified in the brief. Likes need a uniqueness constraint so retries do not inflate counts.

decision.question: How do we support replies, likes, and changing pages without claiming an unspecified ranking rule?
decision.chosen: Persist parent/root links and unique likes; use keyset cursors for chronological reads and keep top ranking gated on a product-defined score and freshness policy.
decision.chosenReason: This supports the stated thread and ordering needs while keeping duplicate retries and page movement bounded.

alternatives.option: Use offset pagination over a mutable global list
alternatives.tradeoff: Deep pages become expensive and concurrent inserts can repeat or skip comments.

alternatives.option: Use nested-set positions as the only reply representation
alternatives.tradeoff: Insertions can require broad position updates; parent/root links are easier to maintain under concurrent replies.

steps.title: Add a bounded thread-page cache
steps.content: Cache only bounded, versioned thread pages or hot roots, keyed by post, order mode, cursor, and visibility scope. Use short, measured lifetimes and invalidation from committed changes. Do not cache private or pending comments into a public key, and do not make the cache authoritative for likes or comment existence.

component.label: Hot Thread Page Cache
component.description: Bounded cache for popular posts and thread pages

properties.purpose: Cache bounded, versioned approved-thread pages for hot posts by visibility scope, sort mode, and opaque cursor; apply short measured TTLs and invalidation, and allow safe database fallback on miss, staleness, or eviction.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Cache component for replaceable read acceleration.

steps.title: Connect bounded reads to the cache
steps.content: Read a matching approved page from cache when its version and visibility key are valid; otherwise fetch from the system of record and repopulate within size and TTL limits. Cache errors must not block a correct page read.

connection.label: Versioned page lookup and invalidation
connection.description: Cache accelerates approved thread reads; durable storage remains authoritative.

steps.title: Define the cache-miss fallback
steps.content: On a cache timeout, eviction, stale version, or invalidation delay, serve the authorized page from durable storage using the same cursor and ordering contract. If top-order materialization is stale, report its freshness or temporarily fall back to chronological order only if product accepts that behavior; never label a stale rank as current. Apply backpressure before falling back if the database is already saturated.

steps.title: Scale from measured hot-post pressure
steps.content: Do not choose shard counts from daily volume alone. Measure peak writes, per-post skew, query fan-out, cache hit rate, page latency, and storage limits before selecting partitioning or read replicas.

scaleTrigger.metric: Per-post write rate, database saturation, cursor-page latency, cache hit rate, and shard skew
scaleTrigger.action: Increase service capacity and add or rebalance measured post/time partitions; preserve deterministic cursor merge and permission checks.
scaleTrigger.impact: Raises throughput while retaining stable page semantics; repartitioning and cross-shard reads add operational and query cost.

steps.title: Add a durable moderation queue
steps.content: Queue moderation requests from committed outbox rows. Partition by post or another measured key, keep retries bounded, and send poison or exhausted jobs to a dead-letter path for inspection. Queue acknowledgement follows durable handoff to the moderation worker; a queue outage must leave work recoverable in the outbox.

component.label: Durable Moderation Queue

properties.purpose: Carry idempotent moderation jobs from committed outbox records with bounded retries, per-post ordering where needed, lag visibility, and a dead-letter path; never serve as the durable source of comment state.

component.highlightReason: Uses the catalog Message Broker for asynchronous durable work.

steps.title: Add the moderation worker
steps.content: Apply the product-approved spam and profanity policy to a versioned comment. The worker must be idempotent, record the policy/version and outcome, and move uncertain cases to review rather than publishing them. It updates the authoritative comment status before creating a publishable change event.

component.label: Comment Moderation Worker
component.description: Idempotent policy checks and status transitions

properties.purpose: Run the approved spam/profanity policy idempotently, record policy version and reason, move uncertain outcomes to review, update durable status before fanout, and retry transient failures without exposing pending content.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Processing Worker for asynchronous moderation.

steps.title: Deliver moderation jobs to workers
steps.content: The worker claims each job with a lease or broker visibility timeout, checks the comment version before applying a result, and acknowledges only after its durable state transition succeeds. Duplicate deliveries are expected and harmless.

connection.label: At-least-once moderation jobs
connection.description: Versioned, idempotent work with bounded retries and dead-letter handling.

steps.title: Commit moderation outcomes to the system of record
steps.content: The worker conditionally changes only the expected comment version. Approval, rejection, or hold state and the corresponding event intent commit together, so a stale moderation result cannot resurrect an edited or deleted comment.

connection.label: Conditional status and outbox transaction
connection.description: Persist moderation outcome and publish intent atomically against the expected comment version.

steps.title: Add an outbox relay
steps.content: The relay claims committed outbox rows, publishes moderation requests to the durable queue and approved/edit/delete/like events to the live event fabric, then marks each row delivered. Use retry with backoff and idempotent event IDs; keep the database outbox until delivery is confirmed. This avoids a database-plus-broker dual-write gap.

component.label: Comment Outbox Relay
component.description: Retryable publication of committed state changes

properties.purpose: Claim committed transactional outbox rows, publish moderation jobs and versioned visible-change events with stable IDs, retry with backoff, and mark delivery only after broker acknowledgement; recover safely after restart.

component.highlightReason: Reuses the catalog Processing Worker for reliable publication.

steps.title: Read and checkpoint committed outbox rows
steps.content: The relay claims rows in bounded batches and checkpoints delivery per event ID. Expired leases are reclaimable after a crash; retries do not remove the source row or create a second logical event.

connection.label: Leased outbox scan
connection.description: Bounded, checkpointed reads and delivery state for committed event intents.

steps.title: Route outbox moderation requests durably
steps.content: Only moderation requests are sent to this queue. The relay retries a broker outage from the outbox; it does not mark the row delivered before the queue confirms receipt.

connection.label: Durable moderation requests
connection.description: Outbox-backed, idempotent jobs; queue outages are recovered by relay retry.

steps.title: Add the live event fabric
steps.content: Publish only committed, visible state changes. Include post ID, comment ID, event ID, entity version, and sequence information needed for deduplication and gap detection. Partition or route by post where ordering is required, and set retention from a product-approved recovery window.

component.label: Approved Comment Event Fabric
component.description: Fanout of committed visible comment changes

properties.purpose: Fan out committed approved, edited, deleted, and like-count changes with stable event IDs and entity versions; route by post where ordering is needed and expose lag without becoming the comment system of record.

component.highlightReason: Uses the catalog Pub/Sub component for event distribution.

steps.title: Publish visible changes after commit
steps.content: The relay publishes approved changes only after the database transaction commits. Rejected and pending comments never enter the public post stream; authorized moderation tooling can use a separate access-controlled path.

connection.label: Committed visible-change events
connection.description: Versioned event publication from the durable outbox after state commit.

steps.title: Add the WebSocket delivery tier
steps.content: Terminate authenticated long-lived connections separately from comment storage. Keep connection state replaceable, bound subscriptions and outbound buffers, and recheck post visibility when a subscription is established or access is revoked.

component.label: Live Comment WebSocket Gateways
component.description: Authenticated subscriptions and bounded event delivery

properties.purpose: Maintain replaceable authenticated connections, authorize each post subscription, bound per-connection queues and subscription counts, deliver versioned visible events, and support resubscribe plus catch-up after disconnect.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Web Server component to host the WebSocket delivery tier.

steps.title: Fan out events to subscribed gateways
steps.content: Gateways subscribe to the event partitions needed by their active post rooms. Enforce a bounded buffer and deduplicate by event ID/version; a disconnected client can recover from its last cursor instead of requiring unbounded server-side buffering.

connection.label: Post-scoped event fanout
connection.description: Versioned events delivered to authorized rooms with bounded buffering and deduplication.

steps.title: Open an authorized live subscription
steps.content: The client sends its post ID and last applied event cursor after authentication. The gateway validates current post visibility and subscription limits before joining a room; the cursor is a recovery position, not an authorization token.

connection.label: Authenticated post subscription
connection.description: Client provides post ID and last event cursor; gateway rechecks visibility and limits.

steps.title: Deliver ordered, deduplicable updates
steps.content: Send the event ID and entity version with each update. The client ignores duplicates, detects version gaps, and requests catch-up instead of assuming transport delivery is exactly once.

connection.label: Live approved comment updates
connection.description: Versioned events; clients deduplicate and detect gaps before rendering.

steps.title: Make visibility a deliberate moderation decision
steps.content: The brief requires spam and profanity filtering but does not define its policy or review workflow. Keep new comments pending until the approved policy returns an allow result; uncertain and unavailable outcomes remain hidden and can be reviewed. The author may see pending status, but other subscribers receive no content event until approval commits.

decision.question: What happens before a comment passes moderation?
decision.chosen: Persist it as pending, show that state only to its author, and publish content only after a durable approved transition.
decision.chosenReason: This makes the moderation boundary explicit and prevents a retry or policy timeout from leaking unreviewed text.

alternatives.option: Broadcast immediately and retract rejected comments later
alternatives.tradeoff: Clients can see content that moderation later rejects; deletion cannot undo screenshots or notifications.
The user receives no recoverable state and retries can create confusion; a held state and review path are auditable.

steps.title: Recover missed live events with a cursor
steps.content: WebSockets are a low-latency hint channel, not the only way to recover state. On disconnect, the client reconnects with backoff, reauthenticates, resubscribes, and fetches the authorized thread after its last applied cursor. If event retention has expired or a sequence gap cannot be filled, reload a fresh page from the system of record and replace local state.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Choose safe behavior for storage and queue outages
steps.content: The database is authoritative, and the outbox is the durable bridge to asynchronous work. Define acknowledgements and fallback behavior before tuning retries.

decision.question: What do users see when storage, the queue, or live delivery is unavailable?
decision.chosen: If the database transaction fails, do not acknowledge the write. If storage commits but the queue is down, retain the outbox row and show the comment as pending. If WebSockets are down, provide authorized cursor-based reads and reconnect/catch-up.
decision.chosenReason: This avoids false success, lost moderation work, cache-only writes, and dependence on a live socket for correctness.

alternatives.option: Acknowledge from cache while storage is unavailable
alternatives.tradeoff: The cache can evict or lose the write, so the user may be told a comment exists when it does not.

alternatives.option: Skip moderation or publish directly when the queue is down
alternatives.tradeoff: A transient infrastructure failure would bypass a stated moderation requirement.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Make edit and delete races safe
steps.content: Edits increment a version and re-enter the moderation policy if changed text can affect visibility. Deletes write a tombstone with actor, version, and timestamp rather than removing ordering history immediately. A moderation result for an older version cannot overwrite a newer edit or delete. Emit the committed change through the outbox and invalidate affected cached pages.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Scale fanout for a viral post
steps.content: Thousands of comments on one post can create hot partitions and a large live room. Do not fan out to every follower; deliver only to currently authorized viewers who subscribed to that post. Keep write acceptance independent from best-effort presence state.

scaleTrigger.metric: Per-post publish rate, active authorized subscriptions, gateway buffer growth, hot-partition load, and event lag
scaleTrigger.action: Split hot-post work across measured partitions and gateway shards; coalesce replaceable count/presence updates, while preserving each comment event or making it catch-up discoverable by cursor.
scaleTrigger.impact: Reduces hot-room pressure but adds partition coordination and catch-up work; coalescing must never hide a committed comment.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Set a moderation backlog response
steps.content: Track oldest pending age and moderation queue lag, not just queue depth. Pending content stays hidden from other users while the worker fleet catches up.

scaleTrigger.metric: Oldest moderation-job age, queue lag, worker error rate, and pending-comment age
scaleTrigger.action: Scale workers within policy limits, alert operators, and apply explicit retry-later admission control if the approved pending-age threshold is exceeded; route exhausted jobs to review.
scaleTrigger.impact: Protects the moderation boundary and makes latency degradation visible; a product-approved threshold is needed before automatic rejection or pause behavior is enabled.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Fail closed when moderation is unavailable
steps.content: A policy service timeout, worker crash, or unknown policy version leaves the comment pending and not publicly broadcast. Retry transient failures with bounded backoff, then route to an authorized review queue. Do not silently approve as a fallback. Any automated policy or human-review threshold is a product decision and should be versioned and audited.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Protect privacy and mutation integrity
steps.content: Authorize reads, subscriptions, edits, deletes, and moderation actions against current post visibility and actor roles. Keep credentials out of events and logs; bound comment text, nesting depth if product defines a limit, subscription count, and outbound buffers. Revoke or remove subscriptions when post access changes. These controls are assumed integrations and service responsibilities, not new requirements from the frozen brief.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Add end-to-end operational monitoring
steps.content: Correlate request, comment, event, and post IDs without logging raw comment text. Monitor user-visible latency and correctness, not only process health. Alert on lost-progress signals such as stuck outbox rows, moderation age, event lag, cursor-gap recovery, and cache fallback saturation.

component.label: Comment Reliability Monitoring
component.description: Latency, queue, moderation, cache, and delivery signals

properties.purpose: Correlate request, comment, event, and post identifiers while excluding raw text; track read/write latency, moderation age, outbox and event lag, cache fallbacks, WebSocket gaps, throttles, and error rates.

component.highlightReason: Uses the existing Monitoring component for service-level and pipeline health.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe comment API health
steps.content: Measure end-to-end create/read latency, authorization denials, idempotent retries, and cursor-page size. Avoid recording comment bodies or access tokens in traces.

connection.label: Service metrics and traces
connection.description: Latency, errors, retries, authorization outcomes, and bounded-cardinality identifiers.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe durable storage pressure
steps.content: Track transaction conflicts, hot partitions, replication health, query latency, and capacity headroom. Alert before the database fallback path saturates during cache trouble.

connection.label: Storage health signals
connection.description: Transaction, query, replication, partition skew, and capacity telemetry.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe moderation queue lag
steps.content: Measure oldest-job age and retries per partition, and verify dead-letter items have an owned review path. A healthy broker process does not imply that comments are being moderated promptly.

connection.label: Queue lag and retry signals
connection.description: Oldest age, per-post lag, retry count, and dead-letter volume.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe moderation outcomes
steps.content: Track policy version, approval/rejection/hold counts, worker age and errors, and stale-version conflicts. Restrict access to moderation evidence and exclude raw text from general telemetry.

connection.label: Moderation health signals
connection.description: Outcome counts, policy version, worker errors, holds, and stale results.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe outbox delivery progress
steps.content: Alert on the age of the oldest undelivered row, lease churn, publish retries, and event-ID duplicates. This reveals a broken live path even when comment writes continue succeeding.

connection.label: Outbox progress and publish retries
connection.description: Undelivered age, lease recovery, broker acknowledgements, and duplicates.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe live connection health
steps.content: Measure authorized active subscriptions, reconnect rate, event-to-client delay, slow-consumer drops, and catch-up success. Treat a gateway buffer limit as a reason to recover by cursor, not to claim the client received every frame.

connection.label: Connection and delivery metrics
connection.description: Subscription counts, delivery delay, reconnects, bounded-buffer pressure, and catch-up.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Observe cache fallback pressure
steps.content: Track hit rate, stale-version rejects, invalidation delay, evictions, and database fallbacks. Alert on a miss storm before a correct cache bypass turns into an overloaded system-of-record incident.

connection.label: Cache and fallback signals
connection.description: Hit rate, invalidation delay, eviction, stale entry, and fallback volume.

steps.phase: Operate under failures and viral load
steps.title: Review unresolved product and capacity decisions
steps.content: Before launch, confirm the top-ranking formula and freshness, maximum nesting depth, peak per-post and aggregate write rates, comment and event retention, numeric latency/availability targets, moderation policy and review ownership, and behavior when moderation age exceeds its threshold. Validate partition and cache choices with skewed viral-post load. The design preserves durable state and recoverable delivery, but the brief alone is not enough to claim a particular throughput, latency, or availability result.
